title: Mixed-workload harness for continuous-batching and queueing analysis
creator: Aisha R. Chen
description: Goal: Build a repeatable load-testing harness that stresses continuous-batching + request queuing under realistic mixed traffic patterns and surfaces tokens/sec, p95 latency regressions, and queueing-induced tail effects. Scope includes: arrival pattern generator (Poisson + bursty), mixed workload profile (short chatty requests, medium multi-turn, long-context completions, background embedding requests), KV-cache hit/miss correlation, per-request queue depth tracing, and an automated regression detector that runs nightly against baseline artifacts.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha R. Chen: Created ticket. Initial plan attaches to runtime-1.21 release for performance validation before rollout. Suggested workloads: 40% short (<=64 tokens), 40% medium (256-1024 tokens), 20% long (2k-8k tokens).

2026-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Poisson arrival generator prototype ready in bench-utils (branch: feat/mixload-arrival). Early runs show continuous-batching increases throughput but p95 degrades for short requests during burst windows.

2026-03-03 - Priya Kapoor (SRE): Observed autoscaler cooldown (default 60s) causing queue buildup during ramp-downs. Recommend adding an experiment that disables autoscaling to isolate runtime behavior from infra scaling artifacts.

2026-03-05 - Diego Martinez: Ran isolated single-GPU experiments with autoscaler disabled. Findings: enabling continuous-batching (max_batch_wait_ms=12) improved tokens/sec by ~30% for steady arrival, but p95 for short requests increased by ~18ms during 5s bursts. KV-cache warm vs cold runs moved p95 by an additional +25ms for long-context flows.

2026-03-08 - Evan Liu (Bench eng): Implemented trace correlation: each request now emits queue_depth and batch_id. Added Grafana dashboard panel for 95th queue_depth and batch_size distribution. Initial dashboard links below.

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Integrated regression detection job in CI. Using bootstrap-based significance test comparing nightly run vs baseline for three primary signals: cluster tokens/sec, p95 latency (by slice), and max queue_depth. Alerts will create ENG tickets if p-value < 0.01 and effect size > 10%.

2026-03-12 - Aisha R. Chen: Review feedback from PM/Perf: include a canary mode that runs the harness with 'SLO-first' batching (prefer lower p95 over throughput) to produce candidate configurations for runtime-1.21 rollout. Added as follow-up action.
metrics_summary: Representative baseline (single A100 equiv GPU, model redwood-base-8k-q4): steady mixed load produced 1350 tokens/sec (per-GPU median), cluster aggregate ~13,500 tokens/sec at 10 GPUs. Median latency=14ms, p95 latency=92ms in steady-state with KV warm. Under 10s bursty arrivals (2x peak rate) queue_depth 95th jumped to 48 requests and p95 latency to 210ms. Continuous-batching with max_batch_wait_ms=12 increased tokens/sec by 28% on average but added +12ms p95 for short requests during bursts. Disabling autoscaling removed a confounder but showed queueing behavior still present due to batch sizing heuristic.
experiments: E1: Arrival distributions - Poisson, bursty (Pareto burstlets), and scheduled ramp - measure tokens/sec and p95 per-slice.
E2: Batching knobs sweep - max_batch_wait_ms {2,6,12,20}, max_batch_tokens {1024,2048,4096} - measure throughput vs p95 trade-offs.
E3: KV cache warm vs cold - run paired experiments to measure delta in p95 for long-context workloads.
E4: Autoscaler interaction - compare runs with cluster autoscaling enabled vs static capacity to isolate orchestration effects.
E5: SLO-first mode - enforce batch sizing policy that prioritizes p95 budget and record throughput loss.
E6: Regression detector sensitivity - synthetic perturbations (inject +15% kernel latency) to validate nightly alerting thresholds.
decisions: D1: Use mixed workload profile (40/40/20 short/medium/long) as canonical baseline for this project.
D2: Implement arrival generator that supports Poisson + configurable burstlets (Pareto) and deterministic replay for CI reproducibility.
D3: Regression detection will be bootstrap-based with two-sided test, p-value threshold 0.01 and minimum relative change 10% before auto-ticketing.
D4: Instrumentation contract: each request must emit queue_depth, batch_id, batch_size, kv_hit boolean, and tokens_produced for post-run slicing.
D5: Add a canary 'SLO-first' configuration to accompany throughput-max configs during runtime rollouts.

AI-2: (Evan) Add queue_depth and batch_size panels to the existing mixload Grafana dashboard; provide snapshot links for baseline runs.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Harness can replay deterministic mixed workloads and emit per-request traces (queue_depth, batch_id, kv_hit, tokens).
AC2: Nightly regression job runs against canonical baseline and opens ENG tickets on statistically significant regressions per rules in D3.
AC3: Grafana dashboard shows tokens/sec, median/p95 by slice, batch_size distribution, and 95th queue_depth for each run.
AC4: At least one SLO-first configuration exists and its trade-offs are documented for runtime-1.21 rollout decisions.
AC5: Documented experiment results (E1-E6) uploaded to Confluence with interpretation and recommended defaults.
